body:
First-touch (triage): promoted `pm:queue`, `domain:engine`, Bug — the last unscoped introspection arm; fix shape is the family's existing pin (`AND tc.table_schema = ANY (current_schemas(false))`), keeping one resolution rule across the four arms. The live-PG test isolation (#9350, per-file schemas in one database) makes name collision the normal state of a test run, so a regression pin against two same-named tables in different schemas is in scope. Serial: `sql-driver.ts` is hot (#11161 in flight, #11223/#11224 queued this round) — the engine seat owns the five-gate fold-or-serial answer across the family at claim time.

**Claim** — engine seat, session `session_01RfyXxZ2WPjcjhuXpiQQc3y`, branch `claude/issue-11201-introspect-fk-schema-scope`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in one label write, read back.

## Correction: this card was held earlier today on a mis-measurement — mine

At ~10:07 I recorded, on the seat post, that #11201 would not be dispatched because `introspectForeignKeys` "is exactly the region #11270 is rewriting". **That was wrong, and the way it was wrong is worth recording.** I read the word `foreignKeys` in #11270's PR body — where it appears in a sentence describing which *extra keys the interface carries* (`isUnique`, `maxLength`, `foreignKeys`, `primaryKeys`) — and treated a prose mention as a region reading. I never opened the diff.

Measured now, on the actual patch (`origin/main...96b4153c`):

| PR | hunks in `sql-driver.ts` | what they are |
|---|---|---|
| #11270 (parked draft) | 3673–3697, 3702–3715, 3722–3729, 12925–12934 | the three `Omit` interface declarations + one column-type site |
| #11224 (in flight) | ~5937 `updatedAtStamp()` and call sites 6139 / 7100 / 7155 | write-door stamp |
| **#11201 (this card)** | **13137 `introspectForeignKeys` body, call site 10324** | the `information_schema` WHERE clause |

`introspectForeignKeys` is ~200 lines below #11270's nearest hunk and in a different method. The three regions are disjoint. The serialization carve-out applies as written — a clearly-stated region does not force whole-file serialization — and #11270's body states its region precisely.

Two things made the wrong hold more expensive than a simple miss: #11270 is **parked as a draft until the cloud-side reading on seam card #11232 posts clean**, so the hold I placed had no bounded exit; and the failure shape is the one already recorded on #11223 this term — inheriting a claim and dressing it in the language of measurement. A region claim is a measurement claim. The diff is cheap; I should have read it the first time.

## H17 trigger-file check — no rider owed

Two `pm:on-hold` cards declare this file as their trigger, and **both scope the trigger to a function, not the file**: #8740 names the *upsert region* / `insertOnlyUpsertColumns`; #6009 names `sqliteCanonicalDatetimeSql`. This change touches neither. The discipline is already on record at #6009 (2026-08-07): *"read the patch rather than the file list, because restart condition 2 is about one function, not the file"* — and, explicitly, *"a `sql-driver.ts` commit in the log is not by itself a trigger for this issue."* A courtesy touch-notice will be posted on both cards once the PR number exists.

## Scope

Not Clause ②: `packages/spec` is untouched, `IntrospectedForeignKey`'s shape does not change, and the accepted set is not widened — a same-named table in another schema ceases to contribute foreign keys it never should have contributed. That is `declared = enforced` restored, i.e. a Bug fix, dispatched at the standard tier.
